# React 18 to 19 Migration

Covers dimension 5: breakages, deprecated patterns, ecosystem compatibility.

For source details, see [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Recommended Upgrade Path

1. Upgrade to **React 18.3** first [2]
2. React 18.3 is identical to 18.2 but adds deprecation warnings for React 19 changes [2]
3. Fix all warnings in 18.3
4. Run codemods
5. Upgrade to React 19

## Codemods

### JavaScript Migration Recipe

```bash
npx codemod@latest react/19/migration-recipe
```

Runs these codemods [2]:
- `replace-reactdom-render`
- `replace-string-ref`
- `replace-act-import`
- `replace-use-form-state`
- `prop-types-typescript`

### TypeScript Codemods

```bash
npx types-react-codemod@latest preset-19 ./path-to-app
```

Includes [2]:
- `no-implicit-ref-callback-return`
- `refobject-defaults`
- `react-element-default-any-props`
- `scoped-jsx`

## Removed APIs

All removed APIs were deprecated years ago [2]:

| API | Deprecated Since | Replacement |
|-----|-----------------|-------------|
| `PropTypes` | April 2017 (v15.5.0) | TypeScript / ES6 defaults |
| `defaultProps` (function components) | — | ES6 default parameters |
| Legacy Context (`contextTypes`, `getChildContext`) | October 2018 (v16.6.0) | `React.createContext` |
| String refs | March 2018 (v16.3.0) | Ref callbacks or `useRef` |
| Module pattern factories | August 2019 (v16.9.0) | Regular function components |
| `createFactory` | February 2020 (v16.13.0) | JSX |
| `ReactDOM.render` | March 2022 (v18.0.0) | `createRoot` |
| `ReactDOM.hydrate` | March 2022 (v18.0.0) | `hydrateRoot` |
| `unmountComponentAtNode` | March 2022 (v18.0.0) | `root.unmount()` |
| `findDOMNode` | October 2018 (v16.6.0) | Refs |
| `react-test-renderer/shallow` | — | `react-shallow-renderer` package |
| UMD builds | — | ESM CDN (e.g., esm.sh) |

Additionally removed unstable APIs [2]:
- `unstable_flushControlled`
- `unstable_createEventHandle`
- `unstable_renderSubtreeIntoContainer`
- `unstable_runWithPriority`

## New Deprecations in React 19

| API | Status | Replacement | Source |
|-----|--------|-------------|--------|
| `forwardRef` | Deprecated | `ref` as prop | [1][2][24] |
| `<Context.Provider>` | Deprecated (future removal) | `<Context value={...}>` | [1][2] |
| `element.ref` | Deprecated | `element.props.ref` | [2] |
| `react-test-renderer` | Deprecated | `@testing-library/react` | [2] |
| `useFormState` | Renamed | `useActionState` | [1][2][12] |

## TypeScript Breaking Changes

### Ref Callback Returns

Ref callbacks cannot implicitly return values (for cleanup function support) [2]:

```tsx
// ❌ Breaks in React 19
<div ref={current => (instance = current)} />

// ✅ Required
<div ref={current => { instance = current }} />
```

### useRef Requires Argument

`useRef()` now requires an argument (can be `undefined`) [2]:

```ts
// ❌ Errors
useRef();
createContext();

// ✅ Required
useRef(undefined);
createContext(undefined);
```

All refs are now mutable; `MutableRef` deprecated in favor of `RefObject<T>` [2].

### ReactElement Props Type

`ReactElement["props"]` defaults to `unknown` instead of `any` [2].

### JSX Namespace

Global `JSX` namespace removed; use `React.JSX` [2].

### useReducer Types

`useReducer<React.Reducer<State, Action>>(reducer)` pattern breaks. Use contextual typing: `useReducer(reducer)` [2].

## Behavioral Changes

### Error Handling

- Errors in render no longer re-thrown — uncaught errors go to `window.reportError` [2]
- Error Boundary-caught errors logged once via `console.error` (not 3 times) [2]
- New callbacks: `onCaughtError`, `onUncaughtError` on `createRoot`/`hydrateRoot` [2]

### New JSX Transform Required

React 19 requires the modern JSX transform (introduced 2020). Error if not enabled: "Your app is using an outdated JSX transform" [2].

### Suspense Fallback Behavior

Fallbacks commit immediately when a component suspends, without waiting for sibling tree [2]. This is faster but changes the order of operations for some patterns.

### StrictMode

`useMemo` and `useCallback` reuse results from first render during second render (new in 19). Ref callbacks double-invoked to simulate Suspense replacement [2].

### JavaScript URLs

`javascript:` URLs now error in `src` and `href` attributes [2].

### Libraries Using React Internals

Libraries depending on `SECRET_INTERNALS_DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED` may break. Field renamed to `_DO_NOT_USE_OR_WARN_USERS_THEY_CANNOT_UPGRADE` [2].

| React 19.2.4 | January 26, 2026 | DoS mitigations | [37] |

## Adoption Data

From the State of React 2025 survey (3,760 respondents, Nov 2025–Jan 2026) [20]:

- **48.4%** daily usage of React 19 within months of release
- **41%** remain on React 18
- Reasons for staying on 18: large codebases, Server Component concerns, ecosystem library compatibility

## Ecosystem Compatibility

### Framework Support

| Framework | React 19 Support | Notes | Source |
|-----------|-----------------|-------|--------|
| Next.js 15+ | ✅ | App Router uses React 19; Pages Router backward-compatible with 18 | [45] |
| Next.js 16 | ✅ | React 19.2 support, compiler integration | [4] |
| Expo SDK 54+ | ✅ | Compiler enabled by default | [47] |

### Testing Migration

- `react-test-renderer` deprecated → migrate to `@testing-library/react` [2]
- Shallow rendering removed → use full component tree with mocked dependencies [2]
- `act` import moved: `react-dom/test-utils` → `react` [2]

## Gaps and Limitations

- No quantitative data on what percentage of React 18 apps can migrate with codemods alone
- Library ecosystem compatibility matrix rapidly evolving; current status of specific libraries requires checking each library's releases
- Enterprise migration timelines and team-size-adjusted effort not published
- Performance comparison between React 18 and 19 for typical applications not benchmarked by React team
